record_body:
Account summary (Dedicated customer) — OrchidPay (orchidpay.com)

Firmographics
- Industry: fintech (payment orchestration + risk ops tooling)
- HQ: NA (US) | Main traffic: us-east-1; secondary: eu-west-1
- Security posture: SOC2 required, SSO/SAML enforced, KMS key separation requested for logs; strong preference for private networking (VPC)

Current Redwood footprint
- Product: Redwood Dedicated (single tenant GPU pool) + limited Hosted API usage for dev/test
- Workloads:
  - Primary: customer support assistant (chat + tool calling) + case summarization
  - Secondary: internal knowledge search (embeddings + rerank)
- Notes on performance: generally happy with p95 latency after batching tuning; occasional spikes during their weekly peak (Mon AM ET). They attribute some of this to their own retry behavior + bursty traffic.

Renewal / renegotiation context
- They are mid-term but requesting a restructure before expansion (finance wants to “clean up” commit before adding capacity).
- Ask: change commit structure from fixed monthly spend to a base commit + burst model (more elastic), with clearer burn-down reporting and ability to shift usage between chat + embeddings/rerank without re-papering.
- Procurement stance: wants any meter-related language in an appendix (“measurement and billing”) + explicit dispute window. They asked whether retries and partial streaming are billable and how we handle disconnects.

Expansion signals
- Product launch planned in March: “agent assist” rollout to ~2x current seats; expecting 1.7–2.3x token volume over 60–90 days.
- New region request: EU volume growing (regulatory pressure + latency); interest in a second Dedicated pool in EU with the same model set.
- Wants to turn on embeddings + rerank at higher volume; currently under-utilizing because of internal spend caps. If we can offer a predictable effective rate, they’ll move doc-search traffic fully onto Redwood.

Pricing sensitivity / commercial notes (highly relevant)
- CFO is pushing hard on effective rate. They benchmarked against:
  - running open models on their own EKS + reserved instances (they cited “unpredictable ops cost + oncall burden” as downside)
  - Bedrock as a fallback option for certain workloads
- They are open to higher total commit ONLY if:
  - we give a step-down in effective blended rate at higher volumes, and
  - we provide a clean story on how batching/caching affects billed units (they worry they’re “paying twice” when they see latency improvements).
- Discounting: they asked if discounts can stack with credits (we told them we need to confirm current policy; they want one approved talk track for their internal finance approval).

Metering + reporting questions (commit burn-down)
- Recurring confusion: commit burn-down vs invoice line items vs console usage page.
  - They want a single monthly CSV that ties: invoice_run_id → meter totals → burn-down summary.
- Specific questions from last call:
  - “If the client disconnects mid-stream, are we billed for tokens the model would have generated anyway?”
  - “Are tokens from our retries counted as new usage? We have aggressive retry logic during 5xx.”
  - “Can we separate billed usage vs failed requests in reporting?”
- Prior ticket (SUP-3129): they raised a mismatch between their internal burn-down calc and our invoice; resolved as an attribution misunderstanding + time window alignment, but they want documentation and contract language tightened.

Key contacts (customer side) — from notes
- VP Engineering (platform): cares about reliability + clean attribution across regions
- Director of Finance: owns commit negotiation and wants predictable spend curves
- Security lead: primarily focused on data retention + audit logs

Recent activity timeline
- 2026-01-29: QBR-style expansion check-in; they flagged March launch volume and asked for commit restructure options.
- 2026-02-06: Finance email follow-up with pricing benchmark questions + request for burn-down examples.
- 2026-02-13: Call (Fireflies ff_a0f3c19d): deep dive on commit burn-down mechanics + batching/caching + metering edge cases; asked for a one-pager they can forward to procurement.
- 2026-02-20: Procurement kickoff scheduled; they requested draft appendix language for “measurement and billing” and clarified dispute window expectations.

Next steps (internal)
- Provide 2–3 commit structures:
  - Option A: base commit + burst priced at a higher marginal rate
  - Option B: two-tier commit with step-down effective rate above threshold
  - Option C: separate regional pools with transferable credits (if Finance approves)
- Include explicit burn-down reporting examples and definitions (billed vs non-billed outcomes, handling of retries, streaming disconnects).
- Loop in Legal for the billing/measurement appendix language and ensure it matches our current meter definitions (avoid anything that implies per-request rounding).

Risk / health
- Expansion probability: high if we land a predictable effective rate + clearer reporting.
- Churn risk: medium if finance concludes cost is non-competitive or if metering explanations remain fuzzy (they are sensitive to anything that looks like over-counting).
